headline: Open models, agent skills, and a free AI course
challenge: Install Ollama, run 'ollama run llama3.3', and ask it to write a Python function that calls an API and parses the JSON response.

items.reason: Open-weight model students can run locally without paid API access.
items.summary: Meta released Llama 3.3 70B, an open-weight model matching closed-model benchmarks, runnable on a single consumer GPU with quantization.
items.why_it_matters: Students can experiment with a top-tier coding model for free on their own hardware.
items.target_audience: CS students, ML researchers, open-source developers
items.what_to_do_next: Run 'ollama run llama3.3:70b-q4' locally and test it on a coding assignment.

items.reason: Free for students, directly improves daily coding workflow with multi-file editing.
items.summary: GitHub Copilot Workspace now supports autonomous multi-file editing from natural language, free for verified students.
items.why_it_matters: Students can describe bugs in plain English and get multi-file fixes across a project automatically.
items.target_audience: All CS students with GitHub Student Developer Pack
items.what_to_do_next: Activate GitHub Student Pack and try Copilot Workspace on your next lab assignment.

items.reason: Directly impacts what skills students need for entry-level SWE jobs.
items.summary: Stanford AI Index reports 62% of entry-level SWE postings now require AI agent or prompt engineering skills.
items.why_it_matters: Shows which skills to prioritize before applying for software engineering internships and jobs.
items.target_audience: Final-year CS students, job seekers, career counselors
items.what_to_do_next: Add an AI agent project to your resume and practice prompt engineering on free platforms.

items.reason: Directly relevant to Indian engineering students facing campus placements.
items.summary: Survey of 200 Indian recruiters shows candidates with AI tool proficiency get 30% higher starting offers.
items.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the salary premium for practical AI skills in Indian campus placement rounds.
items.target_audience: Indian engineering students preparing for campus placements
items.what_to_do_next: Practice live coding with an AI assistant before your next mock interview.

items.reason: Free, fast model with JSON output support, ideal for student API projects.
items.summary: Google DeepMind launched Gemini 2.5 Flash with sub-second latency, free in Google AI Studio with native JSON output.
items.why_it_matters: Students get a free, fast model for building real-time chat and code-completion projects.
items.target_audience: CS students building API-powered projects, hackathon participants
items.what_to_do_next: Sign into Google AI Studio and send your first structured JSON request to Gemini Flash.

items.reason: Duplicate of a05: same Gemini 2.5 Flash release covered by a higher-quality source.
items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Flash for real-time inference with low latency, free via Google AI Studio.
items.why_it_matters: Same release as a05; Hugging Face blog provides more technical depth.

items.reason: Enables free, offline AI coding with local models, eliminating API costs for students.
items.summary: Cursor IDE now supports local Ollama backends, letting students run coding AI entirely offline with open-weight models.
items.why_it_matters: Students can use a professional AI code editor without paying for any API subscriptions.
items.target_audience: Students who want AI coding help without API costs
items.what_to_do_next: Install Cursor, connect it to Ollama, and try side-by-side model comparison on a project.

items.reason: Funding news, not a product feature. No direct student or coding impact.
items.summary: Cursor IDE raised a Series B at $2.5B valuation, planning enterprise expansion with SOC 2 compliance.
items.why_it_matters: Funding rounds don't change the student experience of the free product.

items.reason: Corporate earnings report with zero student coding or career relevance.
items.summary: Nvidia reported Q3 enterprise cloud revenue of $14.2B, up 18%, driven by hyperscaler GPU orders.
items.why_it_matters: No direct impact on student skills, tools, or job readiness.

items.reason: Free, open-source terminal coding agent usable by any student with an API key.
items.summary: OpenAI released Codex CLI, an open-source terminal agent for multi-file edits, test generation, and git integration.
items.why_it_matters: Students gain a free command-line AI coding assistant that integrates directly with their workflow.
items.target_audience: Students comfortable with the terminal, open-source contributors
items.what_to_do_next: Install Codex CLI via npm and try refactoring an existing project from the terminal.

items.reason: Teaches a core technique (RAG) with an open-source pipeline students can replicate.
items.summary: Researchers show RAG reduces hallucinations by 40% across five QA benchmarks, with an open-source pipeline for replication.
items.why_it_matters: RAG is a must-know technique for building reliable AI apps in student projects and interviews.
items.target_audience: ML students, NLP researchers, project teams building AI apps
items.what_to_do_next: Clone the open-source RAG repo and run the notebook on a local dataset.

items.reason: Free, beginner-friendly course by Andrew Ng on the most in-demand AI skill.
items.summary: Andrew Ng and LangChain released a free course teaching students to build AI agents in Python with runnable Jupyter notebooks.
items.why_it_matters: AI agent development is the top skill employers want; this course teaches it for free in under 2 hours.
items.target_audience: Beginners, CS undergrads, anyone preparing for AI interviews
items.what_to_do_next: Enroll at deeplearning.ai and complete the first two modules this weekend.

items.reason: Improves the most popular student editor with better AI integration and Python support.
items.summary: VS Code October update adds inline Copilot Chat with line-by-line diff previews and improved Python venv detection.
items.why_it_matters: Students using VS Code get smarter AI suggestions with more control over accepting or rejecting changes.
items.target_audience: All students using VS Code for coursework
items.what_to_do_next: Update VS Code to v1.95 and try the new inline Copilot Chat on your current project.

items.reason: Unsupported hype claim with no data or peer-reviewed research cited.
items.summary: A startup CEO claims AI will replace 80% of jobs in 3 years, citing no research or data.
items.why_it_matters: Unsubstantiated predictions cause unnecessary anxiety without actionable student guidance.
items.what_to_do_next: Ignore unsupported predictions; focus on building verifiable AI skills instead.

items.reason: Low-quality listicle with no benchmarks, pricing, or comparative analysis.
items.summary: A Medium post lists 50 AI tools with brief descriptions but no benchmarks, pricing, or comparative data.
items.why_it_matters: Lists without analysis waste student time and don't help evaluate tools meaningfully.
items.what_to_do_next: Use curated sources like GitHub Trending or Hugging Face Spaces instead of listicles.
